items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He turned out to be a very good road manager. He knew business, and we work well together. Ed Furst became the road manager, and I, manager.

ctx.x: Ed Fuerst. He hired Ed Fuerst, who had been like one of these groupies. He’d go on the road with us, hang out with us everywhere we played, travel with us. [If] he enjoys a certain food, he’d take George to the – he knew all the restaurants all over the country. He had money. He was well off. And he liked – he wanted to be the road manager. He turned out to be a very good road manager. He knew business, and we work well together. Ed Furst became the road manager, and I, manager. We opened offices in New York.…
Did you – was the transition difficult for you? Did you miss playing?
